name: Muscle-sparing GLP-1 add-ons

lead: GLP-1 receptor agonists such as semaglutide and tirzepatide lower appetite and body weight, and some of the weight lost can be lean mass. Muscle-sparing add-ons are the practices people layer on top, chiefly lifting weights and eating enough protein, to keep as much muscle as possible while losing fat.

The appearance payoff is body composition. Keeping muscle tends to leave a more athletic, firm look at the same scale weight, and it supports strength and metabolism. Several clinical trials of exercise, protein and supplement strategies on GLP-1 drugs are now registered, but results are not yet available.

paras: People on these drugs describe regular resistance training, deliberately reaching a protein target despite lowered appetite, and sometimes easy-to-consume protein such as shakes. Some in forums combine GLP-1 drugs with testosterone replacement or discuss supplements. Trial designs also test hydroxymethylbutyrate (HMB) with vitamin D in older adults.

GLP-1 drugs are prescription medicines with gastrointestinal and other side effects, and a medical provider supervises their use. Reduced appetite can lower protein intake, which is part of the rationale for the add-on strategies. Additional drugs or supplements discussed on forums carry their own risks.

angle.text: People combine resistance training and adequate protein with GLP-1 medication so that weight loss shows up as fat loss with muscle retained, which they see as the difference between looking smaller and looking lean.

lead: Muscle-sparing GLP-1 add-ons are the strategies that people on GLP-1 receptor agonist weight-loss medications use to retain lean mass. The core elements are resistance training and adequate protein, with some adding supplements or hormone therapy.

The connection to looks is composition: weight loss that keeps muscle leaves a firmer, more defined physique than weight loss that includes a large proportion of lean tissue. A 2024 systematic review cited on the semaglutide Wikipedia page found lean mass unchanged in some studies and significantly decreased in others, by 0 to 40 percent, while the ratio of lean to total body mass rose in all of them [1].

Lifters on T Nation forums discuss the issue, including a user citing reports of roughly 40 percent lean mass loss with calorie restriction [2], and members sharing protein and macro approaches while on GLP-1 drugs [3]. A forum post describes a finding that GLP-1 users drop their protein intake by around 25 grams per day [4].
infobox: HMB with vitamin D, protein supplements

paras: GLP-1 drugs such as Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro and Zepbound reduce appetite and lead to weight loss. A T Nation article frames the concern as part of that weight being muscle, which it calls the body's metabolic engine [5]. The add-on strategies aim to reduce that share.

Forum discussions show lifters asking how to preserve muscle on GLP-1 drugs, including a user on testosterone replacement who lifts four days a week and added a GLP-1 drug [6]. Others recommend slow-digesting casein protein for muscle preservation [3]. One poster argued that anabolic drugs build and preserve muscle while GLP-1 drugs help with fat [7].

Several trials of these strategies are registered. NCT07495904 tests the role of dietary protein in maintaining muscle on GLP-1 drugs in 130 adults with obesity [8]. NCT07926152 studies exercise and protein in adults with type 2 diabetes [9]. NCT07760948 tests HMB plus vitamin D in older adults starting semaglutide [10]. NCT07373834 examines tirzepatide and muscle outcomes [11]. A digital resistance-training study in midlife women [12] and a 670-person lifestyle trial [13] are not yet recruiting. Results from these have not been published.
